intro: A text holds together through words that point back (and occasionally forward): pronouns and demonstratives (er, sie, es; dieser, diese, dieses; das / dies for a whole fact; jener, ersterer / letzterer for two items just named), the da(r)-words (damit, dadurch, dabei, danach, darüber, davon, dafür — 'with / through / in / after / about / of / for this'), place and time adverbs (dort, hier, dann, damals), and the connectors that carry the logic between sentences (aus diesem Grund, deshalb, zudem, dennoch, hingegen). A da(r)-word or a demonstrative at the start of a sentence links it to the previous one and sets the verb in position 2. Reading, these words tell you what refers to what — tracking them is how you follow a dense article; writing, they are the difference between a list of sentences and a text. This is the introduction; later in the course you work the full toolkit, including forward reference and paragraph-level cohesion.
tips[0].title: Point back with a pronoun or demonstrative
tips[0].text: Die Stadt baute eine Brücke. Diese / Sie kostete Millionen (a noun → pronoun or dieser). Die Preise stiegen. Das / Dies überraschte niemanden (a whole fact → das / dies). Zwei Optionen, A und B: Erstere ist billig, Letztere schnell (two items → ersterer / letzterer).
tips[0].check.why: The reference is the whole fact that rents rose, so you point back with das. Sie or diese would refer to the rents and need the plural verb überraschten.
tips[1].title: da(r)-words: preposition + 'this'
tips[1].text: damit (with this), dadurch (through this), dabei (in doing so), danach (after that), darüber (about this), davon (of this), dafür (for this), dagegen (against this), daraus (from this). Sentence-initial: verb second. They replace 'mit dem Geld', 'durch das Training', 'bei der Besprechung'.
tips[1].trap: 'with it', 'through it' are two words in English and one in German; and the German one goes first with the verb right after: Damit kaufte er …, not 'Damit er kaufte'.
tips[1].check.why: 'with it' is one word, damit; at the start of a main clause it takes position one and the verb follows immediately.
tips[1].visual.blocks[0].label: the fact
tips[1].visual.blocks[1].label: points back
tips[1].visual.blocks[2].label: points back again
tips[2].title: Logical connectors between sentences
tips[2].text: Cause → Aus diesem Grund / Deshalb. Addition → Zudem / Außerdem / Darüber hinaus. Concession → Dennoch / Trotzdem. Contrast → Hingegen / Dagegen. Time → Danach / Anschließend / Zuvor. Place → Dort / Hier.
tips[2].check.why: The closed road is the cause of being late, so the link is a cause connector: Aus diesem Grund.
tips[3].title: One link per sentence
tips[3].text: Start each new sentence with something that points to the last: a pronoun, a da-word, a connector. If a sentence starts with a brand-new noun and no link, the reader has to work — and the text reads like a list.
tips[3].check.why: Diese points straight back to the new canteen, so the second sentence hooks onto the first. The others start with no link.
remember[0]: Noun → dieser / er; fact → das / dies; two items → ersterer / letzterer.
remember[1]: da(r)-word or connector first, verb second: Damit …, Dadurch …, Dennoch …
mistakes[0].why: Verb second after a fronted da-word.
mistakes[1].why: A whole fact is referred to with das / dies.
hook: Glue your sentences together with das, damit, dabei and dennoch, so a text reads as one argument instead of a list.
